ops.body:
## test_rust_filter_decisions_match_spacy divergence — root cause

**Reproduction:** Test currently PASSES locally (spaCy 3.8.14 + afinn installed; en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 present in ~/.cache/spacy, matching pinned SPACY_MODEL_VERSION="3.8.0"). It did NOT skip — it passes only because real_corpus() sampled transcripts this run that lacked the `Login successful` variant (this run sampled only `<local-command-stdout>(no content)</local-command-stdout>`, no polarity word, so both backends agree). The failure is **flaky by construction**, not fixed.

**Root cause — a tokenizer disagreement between the two backends on XML-tag-glued text.** On `<local-command-stdout>Login successful</local-command-stdout>` (short user text, 2 words <= SHORT_MESSAGE_MAX_WORDS=3), directly reproduced:
- Rust/UDPipe lexicon_has_hit(text, 3, False) = **True**
- spaCy spacy_hit(text, 3, False) = **False**

Mechanism (verbatim token dumps): spaCy en_core_web_sm glues the CLOSING tag into ONE token `successful</local` (opening `<local-command-stdout>Login` splits cleanly, but `word</` stays joined). That token is NOT is_alpha, so `successful` is never scored -> no positive hit. UDPipe english-ewt-ud-2.5 splits `successful` off as its own bare alphabetic token; polarity("successful")=+3 >= floor 3 -> hit. Confirmed: rust lexicon_has_hit("successful</local-command-stdout>", 3, False)=True; lexicon_polarity("successful")=3.

Both backends share IDENTICAL lexicon data: afinn.score("successful")=3.0; generated rust/data/afinn-en-165.tsv + domain_overrides.tsv match installed afinn + DOMAIN_OVERRIDES (both TSV parity tests pass). Python is_alpha and Rust char::is_alphabetic (lexicon.rs:81) are equivalent in intent. The ONLY difference is the token boundary.

**Ruled out:** (a) spaCy model drift — cached model is exactly 3.8.0 == pin; (c) stale generated TSV — data in sync, TSV parity tests green; (d) checked-in fixture staleness — there is NO fixture. real_corpus() samples LIVE ~/.claude/projects transcripts (5 smallest agent- files + a size-spread of others, capped at REAL_CORPUS_SAMPLE), non-deterministic per run and per concurrent-session churn — itself a latent flakiness bug.

**Why CI stays green:** CI lacks the sentiment extra + en_core_web_sm, so @requires_sentiment skips and/or the RuntimeError -> pytest.skip("en_core_web_sm not available") guard fires.

**Deeper issue (not just a test artifact):** `<local-command-stdout>...</local-command-stdout>` and `<command-name>...</command-name>` are Claude Code protocol messages (CC-injected slash-command echoes/output), NOT genuine user prose. The codebase has NO filter for these markers — 0 matches for `local-command`/`command-name` across cc_transcript/*.py; filterspec's CC-protocol text layer covers only denial/interrupt markers. engine.py builds texts from raw UserEvent.text, and ConversationBucketer.bucket_events (buckets.py:57-98) selects all UserEvents filtering only on MIN_USER_CHARS>=5 — no protocol stripping. So these synthetic messages get scored in PRODUCTION too; the parity test merely exposes it.

## Fix options
1. **(RECOMMENDED — fixes the real defect) Strip CC-protocol wrapper messages before sentiment scoring.** Add local-command-stdout/local-command-stderr/command-name/command-message/command-args to the filterspec CC-protocol text layer (parse-once at the owning layer per AGENTS.md). Fixes BOTH the flaky test AND the latent production behavior (CC command echoes must not sway sentiment). Parity test then compares backends on genuine prose only.
2. **Harden backend tokenizer parity directly.** Pre-normalize/strip `<...>` tag syntax before tokenization in BOTH has_hit impls (Rust + Python). Closes the gap generally but touches the Rust-mirrored domain (atomic Rust+Python+parity-repin per AGENTS.md "Rust parity is atomic") and still scores tag-stripped noise — heavier, less correct than #1.
3. **Make the test deterministic + faithful.** Route the corpus through the same protocol/junk filter production uses (once #1 exists), or freeze a hermetic fixture with known-adversarial strings, instead of sampling live transcripts. Kills flakiness; best paired with #1.
4. **(Band-aid) Test-local strip** in corpus_user_texts() only. Cheapest, unblocks the test, but leaves the production noise-scoring gap + backend divergence unaddressed.

**Pick:** #1 (correct owner layer, eliminates the trigger, fixes real product behavior) + #3 (test determinism). #2 is defensible but heavier and still scores noise. Note: task A3 ("generate protocol literals") may be the natural home for #1's marker list — worth coordinating so markers live in one generated source.
